sources: This Is Not a T-Shirt — Bobby Hundreds
Out of the Box — Elizabeth Semmelhack

core_principles.description: Streetwear silhouettes lean oversized on top — one to two sizes larger than your fitted size on shirts, hoodies, and jackets.
core_principles.why_it_works: The oversized silhouette is the visual language of streetwear. It communicates anti-establishment ease and references hip-hop and skate culture origins.
core_principles.when_to_use: Tops, hoodies, graphic tees, sweatshirts in any streetwear outfit.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When the bottom is also oversized or wide — double volume collapses the silhouette.
outfit_examples: Oversized hoodie + slim joggers + Air Force 1s
Oversized graphic tee + slim black jeans + chunky sneakers
Boxy crewneck + tapered cargo pants + Jordan 1s

core_principles.description: If the top is oversized or boxy, the bottom must be slim, tapered, or fitted. Never match volume for volume.
core_principles.why_it_works: The contrast between a relaxed top and a tighter bottom creates a clean, intentional silhouette — the eye reads shape even in loose clothing.
core_principles.when_to_use: Every streetwear outfit with an oversized top piece.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Intentional wide-leg techwear or Korean-influenced wide-wide silhouette (different aesthetic system).
outfit_examples: Oversized Supreme hoodie + slim black jeans + Travis Scott Nike
Large boxy tee + tapered track pants + New Balance 550

core_principles.description: In streetwear, the sneaker is chosen first. The outfit is built around it.
core_principles.why_it_works: Sneaker culture is the origin point of streetwear — the shoe carries the most cultural and aesthetic weight in the outfit.
core_principles.when_to_use: Always when building a streetwear look from scratch.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When you are working with a statement jacket or rare graphic tee that should anchor instead.
outfit_examples: Jordan 4 'Military Blue' → navy + gray + white outfit built around it
Yeezy Foam Runner → monochrome earthy tone outfit to match

core_principles.description: Pull at least one color from the sneaker and repeat it somewhere in the outfit — on the tee, pants, or cap.
core_principles.why_it_works: Creates visual cohesion — the outfit looks intentionally assembled rather than thrown together.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When wearing all-white or all-black sneakers — these are neutrals and need no color pull.
outfit_examples: Jordan 3 'Cardinal' (red detail) → red tee + white shorts + Jordan 3
Nike Dunk 'Panda' (black/white) → all-black outfit or all-white outfit

core_principles.description: A graphic tee is the statement. Everything else in the outfit must be solid — no competing prints or logos.
core_principles.why_it_works: A busy graphic tee needs visual breathing room. Competing patterns create noise that cancels the graphic's impact.
core_principles.when_to_use: Every time a graphic tee is worn as the focal piece.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When layering under an open shirt or jacket — the graphic is partially hidden so conflict is reduced.
outfit_examples: Vintage band tee + solid black cargo pants + clean white sneakers
Supreme box logo tee + solid gray shorts + Jordan 1 Bred

core_principles.description: One visible logo at a time. The most prominent logo should be on the most prominent garment. Avoid stacking chest logo + cap logo + bag logo all in the same sightline.
core_principles.why_it_works: Multiple competing logos create visual noise and undermine each brand's identity. One logo per focal zone.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Head-to-toe branding is an intentional statement look — acceptable if all logos are from the same brand.
outfit_examples: Jordan tee (chest logo) + plain Nike shorts + Air Jordan sneaker (heel logo) — three logos but spatially separated
Off-White tee + plain Carhartt pants + unbranded sneakers

core_principles.description: Core streetwear neutrals: black, white, gray, off-white, beige, and washed tones. These anchor any outfit and let statement pieces lead.
core_principles.why_it_works: Neutrals are the canvas. Statement sneakers, graphics, and logos read clearest against neutral backgrounds.
core_principles.when_to_use: As base garments (pants, plain tees, hoodies) in any streetwear outfit.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When you want a full color-block outfit — intentional deviation from neutrals.
outfit_examples: White tee + black cargo pants + any colorful sneaker
Gray crewneck + beige chinos + Yeezy 700

core_principles.description: Two bold, contrasting colors worn in large blocks — one on top, one on bottom. Keep each block solid with no patterns.
core_principles.why_it_works: Color blocking is visual punctuation. It communicates confidence and references graphic design aesthetics from Supreme, Palace, and Stussy.
core_principles.when_to_use: When you want a bold, high-energy look.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Formal or professional settings. Also avoid more than two bold colors simultaneously.
outfit_examples: Bright orange hoodie + cobalt blue joggers + white sneakers
Red bomber jacket + black trousers + white Air Force 1

core_principles.description: Layer a base tee under a flannel, hoodie, or overshirt, then add an outer jacket. Each layer should be slightly longer than the one beneath it.
core_principles.why_it_works: Visible layering creates depth and signals intentionality. Length staggering makes layering readable — you see each piece.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Summer — single-layer tee outfits are correct for heat.
outfit_examples: White tee + open flannel + denim jacket + black jeans + boots
Black tee + hoodie + puffer vest + joggers + chunky sneakers

core_principles.description: Cargo pants are a functional statement piece. Wear them slightly tapered with an oversized top — avoid very wide cargo + oversized top simultaneously.
core_principles.why_it_works: Cargo pants already carry visual weight through pockets and construction. An oversized top balances the width of cargo without adding competing volume.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Smart casual or any formal context.
outfit_examples: Oversized crewneck + olive cargo pants + Nike ACG boots
Black tee + tapered black cargo pants + white New Balance 990

core_principles.description: Varsity jackets work as the statement outer layer. Keep everything underneath and below simple — solid tee and simple trousers.
core_principles.why_it_works: Varsity jackets are loaded with color and detail (stripes, patches, logos). Everything else must recede so the jacket leads.
core_principles.when_to_use: Autumn and spring streetwear, college-adjacent looks.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Over complex outfits with competing statement pieces.
outfit_examples: Navy/white varsity jacket + white tee + black slim jeans + white Air Force 1
Black/gold varsity + black hoodie (under) + black joggers + Jordan 11

core_principles.description: Hype pieces are trend-driven (collabs, limited drops, seasonal graphics). Timeless streetwear pieces are silhouette- and construction-based (classic crewneck, white tee, Levi's 501, Air Force 1).
core_principles.why_it_works: Building around timeless pieces means your wardrobe has a long shelf life. Hype pieces should accent — not anchor — an outfit.
core_principles.when_to_use: When budgeting a wardrobe — invest in timeless, accent with hype.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Don't build an entire wardrobe around one season's hype items.
outfit_examples: Timeless: White tee + 501 jeans + Air Force 1 (works in any year)
Hype accent: Same base + limited Palace jacket on top

core_principles.description: If you own a rare, loud, or visually complex piece (graphic jacket, bold sneaker collab, heavily printed tee), build the rest of the outfit in plain neutrals.
core_principles.why_it_works: Statement pieces need white space. Surrounding them with neutrals amplifies their impact instead of diluting it.
core_principles.when_to_use: Whenever wearing rare or premium statement streetwear items.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: When you want a balanced, understated look — no statement pieces needed then.
outfit_examples: Takashi Murakami x Louis Vuitton jacket + plain black tee + black joggers + white sneakers
Travis Scott Jordan 1 + beige tee + stone-wash jeans — everything recedes

core_principles.description: Shorts in streetwear should hit just above the knee. Overly long basketball shorts or very short shorts disrupt the streetwear proportion.
core_principles.why_it_works: Above-knee length is the modern streetwear standard — long enough to be functional, short enough to feel contemporary.
outfit_examples: Above-knee mesh shorts + graphic tee + Air Jordan
Cargo shorts (above knee) + oversized tee + Adidas Samba

core_principles.description: A cap (snapback, fitted, 6-panel) should match the dominant or accent color of the outfit. Avoid caps that introduce a completely new fourth color.
core_principles.why_it_works: Headwear is part of the total silhouette in streetwear. An unrelated cap reads as an afterthought rather than an intentional accessory.
core_principles.when_to_use: Any streetwear outfit where a cap is desired.
core_principles.when_to_avoid: Formal adjacent or clean minimal outfits.
outfit_examples: All-black outfit + black New Era fitted
Navy + white outfit + navy snapback

outfit_formulas.formula: Graphic Tee + Slim Black Jeans + White Air Force 1
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: The white sneaker and black jeans are neutral anchors — they let the graphic tee be the only statement. Clean, readable, and endlessly repeatable.

outfit_formulas.formula: Oversized Hoodie + Cargo Pants + Chunky Sneaker
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Oversized top + tapered cargo creates the streetwear silhouette. Chunky sole adds height and visual weight at the base.

outfit_formulas.formula: Varsity Jacket + White Tee + Black Slim Jeans + Clean Sneaker
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: The varsity is the statement. White tee and black jeans are invisible — they exist to frame the jacket.

outfit_formulas.formula: Puffer Jacket + Black Hoodie (under) + Black Joggers + Jordans
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Monochrome black base makes the puffer the only visual event. Jordans break the black with color.

outfit_formulas.formula: Flannel Shirt (open) + White Tee + Dark Slim Jeans + Nike Dunks
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Open flannel acts as a light jacket layer. White tee grounds it. Dunks add the color story.

outfit_formulas.formula: Track Jacket + Plain Tee + Straight Leg Jeans + Adidas Samba
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Track jacket references retro sportswear. Straight jeans are a modern balance. Samba is a clean, classic anchor.

outfit_formulas.formula: Crewneck Sweatshirt + Tapered Chinos + New Balance 990
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Elevated casualwear — the crewneck and chinos lift the look above pure streetwear while the New Balance keeps it grounded.

outfit_formulas.formula: Boxy Tee + Wide Leg Jeans + Low-Top Sneaker
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Wide-wide silhouette works when the tee is boxy (not draped) and the sneaker is low-profile — the flat sole gives visual stability to the wide silhouette.

outfit_formulas.formula: Coach Jacket + Plain Tee + Cargo Pants + Trail Sneakers
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: Coach jacket is a clean, unbranded outer layer. Trail sneakers add technical edge. Cargos bridge utility and streetwear.

outfit_formulas.formula: Denim Jacket + Black Graphic Tee + Black Jeans + Black Boots
outfit_formulas.why_it_works: All-black base with denim jacket on top creates dark sophistication with a streetwear edge. Black boots over sneakers elevate the register slightly.
